sources.entry: Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction by Kieran Healy

summary.name: Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction (2nd ed.)
summary.one_liner: Draft website for Kieran Healy's book teaching data visualization principles and practice in R using ggplot2, forthcoming from Princeton University Press.
use_cases: learning to make graphs in R
summary.what_it_does: This page hosts a complete draft of the second edition of a book on data visualization using R and ggplot2. It introduces perceptual principles of graphics, then walks through building plots layer by layer, from scatterplots and single-variable summaries to faceted plots, derived summaries, maps and model estimates. It also covers refining plots with labels, annotations and themes, and presenting graphics to different audiences. The page gives installation steps for R, RStudio and a list of R packages including tidyverse, ggplot2 support packages and socviz.
notable: Teaches the underlying ideas and code together, with examples built up step by step
Covers ggplot2 version 4 and R 4.5 and the socviz companion package
Includes chapters on maps (sf) and plotting model estimates (marginaleffects)
caveats: The book is not yet available for pre-order; the page only offers a sign-up form for a single notification email
Not a comprehensive R guide or cookbook, and not a statistics text
Requires installing R and RStudio (or another IDE) first
